key_themes: Hot October CPI (core +0.3% vs +0.2% est) reignites Fed rate-hike fears, 10-yr yield near 5%
Earnings season: AAON surges 19% on record sales; Hims & Hers tumbles 17% on EBITDA guide cut
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under board investigation drags AI/chip stocks lower

stocks.discussion_driver: Fell ~5-6% on November 10 as a board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang deepened following reports of an admitted affair and scrutiny of China business ties. The selloff was compounded by hotter-than-expected October CPI data reigniting Fed rate-hike fears, with the 10-year yield near 5%, pressuring high-multiple AI and semiconductor stocks ahead of NVDA's November 17 earnings report.
bull_case: AI chip demand remains strong; data center revenue expected to beat again at the Nov 17 earnings, which could serve as a catalyst to restore investor confidence
Consensus analyst price target of ~$326 implies 93%+ upside from current depressed levels; stock is trading near its 52-week low, potentially offering a long-term entry point
bear_case: CEO Jensen Huang board investigation creates governance uncertainty and potential management distraction during a critical earnings period
Rising 10-year yields near 5% from hot CPI data compress valuations for high-multiple growth stocks; China export restrictions remain an ongoing headwind

stocks.discussion_driver: Surged approximately 19% on November 10 after reporting record Q3 fiscal 2026 sales of $707.4M and raising its full-year 2026 revenue forecast above expectations. Despite the strong beat, Robert W. Baird trimmed its price target from $110 to $104 (keeping Outperform), reflecting caution about near-term valuation after the surge. The stock had declined sharply from its 52-week high of $150.46 prior to earnings, losing over 50% from peak.
bull_case: Record Q3 sales of $707.4M and raised full-year guidance demonstrate strong fundamentals in commercial HVAC and data center cooling demand
Stock remains well below its 52-week high of $150.46 and analyst consensus targets of ~$110 imply meaningful upside even after the post-earnings bounce
bear_case: Despite the 19% surge, stock is still down ~50% from its 52-week high of $150.46, suggesting lingering skepticism about the company's longer-term growth trajectory
Robert W. Baird trimmed its target to $104 post-earnings; declining analyst consensus targets indicate tempered expectations despite the earnings beat

stocks.discussion_driver: Dropped approximately 17% on November 10 after Q3 fiscal 2026 results missed estimates and management slashed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance well below consensus. Revenue guidance was narrowed to $3.13-$3.15B versus the $3.21B analyst estimate. Multiple analysts cut price targets in response — Morgan Stanley to $25, Jefferies to $24, Needham to $32 — while Evercore raised to $27. The stock has now lost nearly 59% from its 52-week high.
bull_case: Despite the guidance cut, revenue guidance midpoint of $3.14B still represents strong growth, and Needham maintained a Buy with a $32 target reflecting long-term telehealth potential
Consensus analyst price target of ~$31.57 implies over 64% upside from post-earnings levels, suggesting the selloff may have been overdone
bear_case: EBITDA guidance cut well below consensus signals margin pressure and execution challenges; Q3 miss raises concerns about scalability and near-term profitability
11 of 15 analysts now rate the stock Hold or Sell; insider selling of ~$6M over the last 3 months suggests limited near-term confidence from management

stocks.discussion_driver: Jumped ~19% in after-hours on November 9 and continued gaining on November 10 after Q3 2026 results beat management's own revenue forecast by $86M despite revenue declining year-over-year for the first time in company history. Management also announced a 15% workforce reduction targeting $100M+ in 2027 savings and issued Q4 revenue guidance above $755M, boosting investor sentiment around a potential profitability recovery.
bull_case: Q3 results beat management's own guidance by $86M; Q4 guidance above $755M and 15% workforce cuts signal commitment to margin recovery in 2027
Connected TV (CTV) and programmatic advertising remain growth vectors; restructuring positions TTD for improved profitability metrics in a recovering ad market
bear_case: Revenue declined year-over-year for the first time in TTD's history, raising fundamental questions about competitive positioning in the evolving ad tech market
Stock is down ~65% year-over-year with a consensus 'Reduce' rating; 26 of 39 analysts rate it Hold or Sell, reflecting persistent skepticism

stocks.discussion_driver: Rose 5%+ on November 9 after JPMorgan added Meta to its Analyst Focus List as a top internet pick, citing AI-driven advertising revenue resilience with an Overweight rating and $940 price target. The move reflects growing confidence that Meta's AI investments are translating into measurable advertising efficiency gains, reinforcing the platform's competitive moat against digital ad rivals amid broader market weakness.
bull_case: JPMorgan's Focus List addition with a $940 target reflects broad analyst consensus — 50 of 57 analysts rate META as Strong Buy or Buy, with a $850+ consensus target implying 32% upside
AI-powered advertising tools, Reels monetization, and Threads growth continue to drive revenue share gains with strong margin expansion
bear_case: Stock trades at a P/E of ~21.6x while facing ongoing antitrust scrutiny and potential regulatory action in the US and EU, which could limit growth or force structural changes
Heavy capital expenditure for AI infrastructure and ongoing Reality Labs losses weigh on free cash flow; a macro slowdown from rising rates could disproportionately hurt digital ad spending
